# URLCode auth

> Operator-installed authentication extension for URLCode. Accounts, sessions,
> roles and an account page for a `urlcode.yaml` project. Node with a patched
> SQLite build; delivered as a signed executable bundle pending independent
> review. Apache-2.0.
>
> Install core from npm, then run `npx urlcode init my-site --with ui,auth`; it
> resolves `extension-bundles@v<core>` unless `--bundle-release` pins another.

Part of the URLCode framework, in the same repository: docs/FRAMEWORK.md

## What a project declares (YAML only; never packages, code or credentials)
- `extensions.auth: { version: "1", config: { registration: "off" | "open" | ... } }`
- A mount: `/account/*: { extension: auth, methods: [GET, HEAD, POST] }`
- Protection: `policies.extensions.auth: {}` on any route that needs a session
- Machine/agent protection: `auth: {bearer: {scopes: [...]}}` on a route instead
  of a session (an operator-issued API key checked against `Authorization:
  Bearer <key>`; issued/listed/revoked outside route YAML via `service.issueApiKey`
  or the `urlcode-auth api-key-issue` CLI). Exclusive of role/permission/verified/
  freshWithinSeconds/onDeny. The verified key's id/name/scopes (never the raw key)
  are exposed to the route's own function/middleware context as base64-encoded
  JSON on the reserved `x-urlcode-context-auth-principal` request header
  (urlcode#618).
- The operator wires `authExtension({ service, csrfKey, projectSha256, ui })` in a host file
  loaded with `urlcode serve --host-file /absolute/host.mjs --origin https://...`
- Presentation: screens are `auth/*` kit templates (`authTemplates`, `authUiTemplates`, `authCatalogue`)
  rendered through `ui.kit.page`. `ui` from `createUiExtension` is required, and `extensions.ui` must be
  declared before `extensions.auth` in `urlcode.yaml`; auth refuses activation otherwise.

## Read in this order
- [README](README.md): signed-bundle install, activation, operator CLI, senders, providers.
- [SECURITY](SECURITY.md) and [threat model](THREAT-MODEL.md): trust boundary; what the extension does not protect.
- [Implementation status](IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md): what is built, what remains.
  The original design spike is private maintainer material.
- [Acceptance](ACCEPTANCE.md), [recovery drill](RECOVERY-DRILL.md): evidence records.

## Do not guess
- No login forms, cookies or password checks in project `function`/`middleware`
  routes; declare the policy. Those routes run trusted and in-process, but hold
  no auth authority of their own.
- `registration` starts off. First administrator: `urlcode-auth bootstrap` with JSON on stdin.
- `inspectExtensionRevision(project)` prints the SHA-256 to pin; inspecting grants nothing.
- Roles are operator configuration; assigning them is an administrative transaction.
- Google/Apple/SES adapters exist but are unverified against live providers.
